## Why Resume Fraud in India Is No Longer a “Rare” Problem


If you think fake resumes are something only large MNCs worry about, the numbers tell a very different story.


According to[AuthBridge’s Workforce Fraud Files H1 FY26](https://authbridge.com/newsroom/workforce-fraud-files-h1-fy26-hiring-discrepancies-india/) , **4.33% of white-collar hires** and **5.61% of gig workforce hires** in India have discrepancies in their background checks. That means roughly **1 in every 20 candidates** you interview is misrepresenting something on their resume.


The problem gets worse in specific industries. AuthBridge’s H2 2025 report found that the **IT/ITES sector** has a staggering **9.46% overall discrepancy rate** , with **18.8% of IT profiles misrepresented** in some form — fake job titles, inflated tenures, fabricated employers. The **telecom sector** isn’t far behind at **11.34%** , with **19% address verification failures** and **6.7% fake education credentials** .


[OnGrid’s FY 2024-25 Annual Report](https://www.ongrid.in/annual-report-fy-2024-25) adds another data point: **3.6 lakh individuals** had at least one background check failure during the year.


### What Resume Fraud Actually Looks Like


Resume fraud isn’t just about fake degrees. Here’s what Indian employers are catching:


Type of Fraud What Candidates Fake How Common How to Catch It


**Employment History Fabrication** Fake company names, inflated tenures, ghost employers Most common — 7% of IT checks fail UAN/EPFO past employment history check


**Salary Inflation** Inflated CTC to negotiate higher offers Very common, hard to detect manually EPFO contribution records via UAN


**Education Fraud** Fake degrees, inflated grades, unaccredited institutions 4.84% of IT checks (AuthBridge) University verification + document OCR


**Identity Fraud** Fake PAN, someone else’s documents Rising with digital job applications PAN/DL/Voter ID government database check


**Moonlighting** Working two full-time jobs simultaneously 4.99% in IT sector (AuthBridge) UAN/EPFO shows overlapping employment dates


### Why Manual Checks Can’t Keep Up


Traditional background verification — calling previous employers, mailing universities, hiring field agents — takes **7 to 15 business days** and costs **₹500–₹2,000 per candidate** . By the time results come back, you’ve already made the offer, the candidate has joined, and if the check reveals fraud, you’re facing an awkward termination.


**Employee past history check software** solves this by pulling verified records directly from government databases — EPFO, Income Tax Department, VAHAN/SARATHI, Election Commission — in **minutes, not weeks** . The best tools don’t just verify what candidates claim; they surface discrepancies that candidates hoped you’d never find.


Here are the **5 best employee past history check software tools** that detect resume fraud instantly in India.

### Why This Matters for Resume Fraud Detection


The **UAN/EPFO past employment history check** is the single most powerful resume fraud detection tool available to Indian employers. Here’s why:

- If EPFO shows an employer the candidate didn’t mention (a gap they tried to hide), you see it.
- If EPFO shows two overlapping employers (moonlighting), the dates speak for themselves.

### 2. How common is resume fraud in India?


Resume fraud is more common than most employers realize. According to[AuthBridge’s Workforce Fraud Files H1 FY26](https://authbridge.com/newsroom/workforce-fraud-files-h1-fy26-hiring-discrepancies-india/) , **4.33% of white-collar hires** and **5.61% of gig workforce hires** show discrepancies. In the IT/ITES sector,[AuthBridge’s H2 2025 report](https://authbridge.com/newsroom/authbridges-workforce-fraud-files-1-in-10-bfsi-job-applications-misrepresented-salary/) found a **9.46% discrepancy rate** , with **18.8% of IT profiles misrepresented** in some form.


### 3. Can software instantly detect if someone faked their employment history?


Yes. SalaryBox Verify’s UAN/EPFO past employment history check pulls a candidate’s actual employment timeline from government records within minutes. This shows every formal employer who contributed to their Provident Fund, with exact joining and exit dates. If the candidate claims 3 years at a company but EPFO shows 11 months, the fraud is immediately visible.


### 4. What is the UAN/EPFO past employment history check and why is it important?


The UAN (Universal Account Number) is linked to every formal employee’s EPFO (Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation) account. It records every employer who contributed to their PF, along with dates of employment and salary brackets. This creates a **government-verified employment timeline** that candidates cannot alter. Checking this record is the most reliable way to detect fake employment history, inflated tenures, and moonlighting in India.


### 5. How much does resume fraud detection software cost?


Costs vary widely. SalaryBox Verify charges **₹26 for PAN verification** and **₹170 for UAN/EPFO past employment history** , meaning basic fraud detection costs just ₹196 per candidate. SpringVerify charges ₹799–₹1,599 per candidate in packages. AuthBridge, IDfy, and SurePass use custom enterprise pricing that requires a sales call.


### 6. What types of resume fraud are most common in India?


Based on AuthBridge data, the most common types are: **employment history fabrication** (fake company names, inflated tenures) — 7% of IT employment checks fail; **salary inflation** (inflated CTC to negotiate higher offers); **education fraud** (fake degrees, inflated grades) — 4.84% in IT; **moonlighting** (working two full-time jobs) — 4.99% in IT; and **address misrepresentation** — 10.11% in IT.


### 7. Can candidates game traditional background checks with fake references?


Yes. Traditional employment verification relies on calling previous employers, and candidates can provide a friend’s number as their “former HR manager.” This is why **government database checks are more reliable** than manual outreach. SalaryBox Verify’s UAN/EPFO check bypasses references entirely — it pulls employment records directly from the government, where candidates can’t plant fake contacts.


### 8. Do I need employee consent before running a past history check?


Yes. Under Indian law, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, employers must obtain **written consent** before conducting any background or employee record check. This applies to identity verification, employment history checks, and criminal record searches. Most verification platforms, including SalaryBox Verify, include consent collection as part of their process.


### 9. How do I detect moonlighting through employee past history check software?


Moonlighting (dual employment) is detectable through the **UAN/EPFO past employment history check** . When an employee works for two companies simultaneously, both employers contribute to their Provident Fund, creating overlapping employment records in EPFO. SalaryBox Verify pulls these records, making overlapping dates immediately visible. AuthBridge’s data shows moonlighting at **4.99% in the IT sector** .


### 10. Is AI-based resume fraud detection better than government database checks?


They serve different purposes. **AI-based fraud detection** (like IDfy) excels at catching forged documents, tampered certificates, and fake ID cards through OCR and image analysis. **Government database checks** (like SalaryBox Verify’s EPFO check) catch the more common frauds: fake employment history, inflated tenures, and salary lies. Since employment fabrication is far more common than document forgery in India, government database checks should be your first line of defense.
